---
title: "Normalize time"
---

![[Normalize Time]{.ui-label} window. Apply a consistent time range across records when time is cumulatively increasing.](images/media/data-tools-normalize-time.png)

The time in electrophysiological data may be recorded in two ways. If 'normalized', the times of each record are the absolute record length (e.g. for $2\ \mathrm{s}$ recordings, record 1: $0$–$2\ \mathrm{s}$, record 2: $0$–$2\ \mathrm{s}$).

Alternatively, time may be recorded relative to the start of recording, increasing cumulatively (e.g. record 1: $0$–$2\ \mathrm{s}$, record 2: $2$–$4\ \mathrm{s}$).

In the case that times are cumulative, [Normalize Time]{.ui-label} normalises them. This is done by replacing the time values for every record with those from the first record, maintaining the [time offset if not corrected on load](loading-files.qmd#correct-non-zero-time-offsets).
